hold_text: PROP-EXEC lane brief (manager session_01HYq6XtfesZ57VyaQrK6CL1): every PR in this lane is held; the manager merges after independent review. Do not arm auto-merge.
why: PROP-EXEC fix-forward #11 (live test #14191, 12:55Z): the order filled and was confirmed with its bracket, but the watched close refused before any click because the hovered Positions row's icon trio sits inside the row's own 'sticky--actions-cell' and CLOSE_ROW_JS's outermost-only filter kept that cell as the row's only control and dropped the icons. Measured by #14198 (dump-tables with the position open): the trio is three text-less <button>s with no title and no aria-label. Fix: a class-only container that holds candidates is descended into and never counted; a control is read by what it SAYS (own + descendants' text / title / aria-label) and what it is CALLED (own + descendants' class / href / data-icon / data-test-id / name, split so 'icon-close' reads as the word close); the x / glyph spellings count from the label only (a class token 'x-small' is not a close), and reverse / modify words anywhere disqualify. Every existing refusal stays: exactly one close-type control, it must be the LAST control of the row, boxed inside the row, away from any canvas; the modal read-back is unchanged. Each control's tag and masked markup now ride the refusal log, and dump-tables prints the position / orders row's control markup (digit runs of 5+ masked) so the next read shows what the icons are called. Replicas in Chromium: the titled trio in the actions cell; the live shape (three text-less buttons told apart by their icon classes) disarmed and armed (Close Position pressed once, reverse / modify never); negatives that press nothing: three nameless buttons, an 'x-small' class token, a close icon inside a reverse-named button, close not last, two close-named icons, and a cell whose only child is the chart x beside a canvas. Round 5: names are split on camelCase as well ('reverseBtn', 'btnReverse', 'Row_reverseButton__a1b2c', 'modifyOrder', 'editPosition', 'closeAll' read their word), data-testid / data-action / id count as names, the row itself keeps the word rule and every ancestor between the control and the row is read by substring like the control; nine armed listener-ancestor replicas (no onclick / tabindex / role, handler by addEventListener, each proven live by a direct click after the refusal) press nothing. Tier 2: the live close path on a funded account; no new click; no sizing, guard or risk change.
